text:
The primary material of a candle is essentially the sound of a Tuesday afternoon, compressed into a wax-like substance that smells faintly of forgotten passwords.

Gerald, who collects nothing but the echo of a sneeze in an empty library, hung ‘The Color of Wind’ on a wall that didn’t exist yet. The painting was so invisible that when he looked at it, his eyes turned inside out to get a better view. He won the auction by bidding with a handful of dry whispers, which the auctioneer accepted as legal tender because the currency had gone on strike for better working conditions.

To celebrate, Gerald hosted a silent dinner party where the guests arrived by leaving. The table was empty, which was perfect, because the chairs were currently in a union dispute over who gets to sit. The food, naturally, was too shy to appear, so everyone ate the concept of hunger instead. It was delicious, mostly because it tasted like the color blue, but only if you blinked in Morse code.
